buttonLabel: "Explore nature in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil and Peru"
lead: >-
  Routes through Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil and Peru bring together three very different natural areas: the humid forest and Iguazú Falls on the Argentina–Brazil border, the salt flats and colorful lagoons of high-altitude Bolivia, and Lake Titicaca and the mountain landscapes of Peru. They are stages of larger multi-country tours, many of which also pass through Chile. Choose based on altitude, duration and the number of days spent in nature, rather than simply the number of countries.
---

## From Iguazú Falls to the high-altitude lakes of the Andes

Our collection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with [Argentina](/argentina/), [Bolivia](/bolivia/), [Brazil](/brazil/) and [Peru](/peru/) among the principal countries. These four do not form a self-contained four-country program. For example, the [18-day five-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) also visits Chile, the [20-day six-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) adds Uruguay, and the [32-day eight-country program](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) covers an even wider geographical area.

What unites their nature-focused sections is a dramatic transition from humid subtropics to cold, high-altitude spaces. At Iguazú, the main attractions are water and forest; in Bolivia, thin air, open horizons and unusual landscapes; in Peru, Lake Titicaca and the high Andean slopes. These stops call for different clothing, physical preparation and planning.

## Argentina and Brazil: the two sides of Iguazú

The shared natural centerpiece of these countries is the Iguazú waterfall system. [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) in Brazil and [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) in Argentina are distinct locations. Our routes visit both countries, and the 32-day program also specifically identifies the [Devil's Throat](/argentina/place/garganta-del-diablo/) as a separate attraction.

Moving from one side of the falls to the other changes the experience. Some viewpoints reveal a broad line of cascades; others bring visitors closer to individual streams and the upper parts of the system. UNESCO describes the neighboring national parks as one natural subtropical forest area spanning the international border. Nevertheless, park entry rules, trail access and cross-border transfers should be checked for the chosen dates rather than assumed to be permanent.

Some itineraries start by the ocean in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). [Tijuca National Park](/brazil/place/tijuca-national-park/) and the slopes of [Sugarloaf Mountain](/brazil/place/sugarloaf-mountain/) introduce the forested, mountainous terrain of a coastal metropolis. But stops in Rio often combine city sightseeing with panoramic viewpoints, so they should not automatically be treated as full forest hikes.

## Bolivia: from the Uyuni Salt Flat to colorful lagoons

In Bolivia, routes pass through [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and high-altitude areas featuring [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and the [Sol de Mañana geysers](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/). This is a completely different kind of landscape from Iguazú Falls. The horizon is often almost treeless, with salt fields, rocky desert and mountain lakes alternating across the terrain.

The salt flat changes appearance depending on surface moisture. Its famous mirror reflection requires a thin layer of water and **cannot be guaranteed on every departure**. Even without it, the vast salt plain remains a compelling destination. To understand this region, consider not only photographs of Uyuni but also the actual hours of driving between lagoons, stops and overnight accommodation.

Most of these tours connect Bolivia with [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) in Chile. Thus selecting these four countries does not eliminate the Chilean section actually traveled. Include it in your calculations of travel time and weather.

## Peru: Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu

After Bolivia, many programs continue to [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). The lake lies high in the Andes, with water, shorelines and island settlements set in a very different climate from Brazil's. Boat visits to the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/) offer a look at how people live on the lake. Check the precise boat itinerary with your selected tour.

The next contrast is [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Machu Picchu combines ancient architecture with a mountain setting. UNESCO recognizes the historic sanctuary for both cultural and natural value; nevertheless, the scheduled visit focuses primarily on the archaeological complex, not an independent trek through all the surrounding mountains.

This Peruvian stage provides a clear conclusion to the journey: from broad salt plains and a high-altitude lake to green slopes and Inca stonework.

## How to compare programs without changing the route

| Main objective | Confirmed places |
|---|---|
| Waterfalls and humid forest | Iguazú, Argentina and Brazil |
| Wide open salt landscapes | Uyuni, Bolivia |
| High-altitude lagoons | Verde and Colorada |
| Geothermal landscape | Sol de Mañana |
| Andean lake | Titicaca, Peru |
| Mountains and Inca history | Machu Picchu, Peru |

When choosing a tour, consider not only the natural attractions but also the pace of the entire program. The [18-day journey](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) links five countries in a relatively tight sequence, the [20-day tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) adds a sixth, and the [32-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) takes the journey farther still. For high-altitude travel, gradual changes in elevation, transfer pace and manageable exertion matter; border-crossing and attraction-entry conditions should be checked for the travelers' nationalities and dates.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki,tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026,tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

To compare all routes without thematic filtering, use the [Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil and Peru catalog](/multi-country/argentina_bolivia_brazil_peru/). For other nature-focused combinations, explore [multi-country nature tours](/multi-country/interests/nature/).

## Frequently asked questions about this nature journey

### Do these tours visit only the four selected countries?

No. The filter shows routes with all four among their principal countries. Some programs also include Chile, Uruguay or other destinations. The complete order of stops is listed on each [multi-country tour](/multi-country/).

### How do the Argentine and Brazilian sides of Iguazú differ?

They offer different views of one waterfall system. The [Brazilian side](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) provides wide panoramas of the cascades; the [Argentine side](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) offers access to other sections of the falls and forest walkways. The availability of individual routes depends on park conditions.

### Can the mirror effect at Uyuni be guaranteed?

No. At [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), reflections depend on surface water. In dry conditions the salt flat looks different, but the natural landscape remains remarkable.

### Does high-altitude Bolivia require special preparation?

Yes. The program includes sections at considerable elevation. Check the travel pace, overnight conditions and how you tolerate altitude before booking. Avoid planning extra exertion immediately after a demanding transfer without taking your well-being into account.

### Is Machu Picchu a nature or history excursion?

[Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) has both kinds of value. The central purpose of the visit on current itineraries is to discover Inca architecture in the mountains, not a promise of a separate, extended mountain trek.

## What “Wildlife and Safaris” means for these four countries

This thematic collection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil and Peru among the principal countries. In the current classification, [the 32-day eight-country route](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) carries “Wildlife and Safaris” as an additional theme. **This is a selection of four countries within a complete itinerary** that also passes through Chile, Uruguay, Ecuador and Colombia. Not every nature tour through these four countries qualifies as a safari.

The nature experiences differ considerably. In Brazil and Argentina, travelers explore Iguazú Falls from opposite sides. In Bolivia, the four-wheel-drive section crosses high-altitude lagoons inhabited by flamingos. In Peru, the program includes Lake Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu; **these are primarily landscapes and cultural sites, not a promised specialist wildlife-watching tour**.

This distinction helps avoid confusing a national park visit with a photographic safari or assuming that one thematic tag guarantees wildlife encounters at every stage. Find all routes without thematic restrictions in the [Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil and Peru catalog](/multi-country/argentina_bolivia_brazil_peru/).

## Brazil: Iguazú and the Atlantic Forest

After the opening days in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the routes continue to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). On the Brazilian side, tourists walk along the cascades and view the falls from broad panoramic platforms. This section reveals the landscape itself: humid tropical forest surrounds the river system, while the viewpoints overlook a long line of waterfalls.

Iguaçu National Park preserves a part of the Atlantic Forest. Many birds and mammals, including rare species, live here, but **neither a general waterfall excursion nor the presence of animals in a park guarantees an encounter with a jaguar or any other particular species**. Sightings depend on the animal's species, timing and behavior, weather, and which visitor routes are permitted.

The [basic 18-day tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) also offers optional visits to the [Bird Park](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/) and a boat trip toward the falls on the Macuco Safari. These are not part of the main excursion, and the word “safari” in the attraction's name does not mean searching for wild animals. The 18-day tour itself is categorized under nature and culture, without a wildlife tag. For comparison, see [“Wildlife and Safaris” tours featuring Brazil](/interests/wildlife/tours/brazil/).

## Argentina: another perspective on the same waterfalls

From Brazil, the group crosses the border and visits the Argentine side via [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). Walkways bring visitors closer to individual cascades, above the water and to the famous [Devil's Throat](/argentina/place/garganta-del-diablo/). This is not a repeat of the Brazilian overview: each side shows the falls from different distances and directions.

The Atlantic Forest continues across the border, so the two days can be understood as an introduction to one cross-border ecosystem. Here, the natural experience centers on the waterfalls themselves and accessible walking routes. Specialized mammal observation, night tours or private wildlife photography are not listed in the published basic program.

After the park, there is a flight to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), where excursions are primarily cultural. For waterfalls and forest scenery, see the [“Nature” collection featuring Argentina](/interests/nature/tours/argentina/); for wildlife observation, consider separate [“Wildlife and Safaris” tours featuring Argentina](/interests/wildlife/tours/argentina/), checking the actual days dedicated to animal viewing.

## Bolivia: high-altitude lagoons and flamingos

After [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), the group crosses into Bolivia and starts a 4×4 jeep route. One of the first stops is [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), followed by thermal fields, geysers and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), where James's flamingos are explicitly mentioned in the itinerary.

This is the clearest activity involving wild birds among the four countries in this collection. It is important to distinguish **habitat from a guaranteed sighting**: flamingos inhabit high-altitude lagoons, but their numbers, distance from the flock and opportunities for photographs vary. Access to the shore and restrictions in the protected area are governed by local rules; free access to birds for photographs cannot be promised.

The next day, the route crosses the Honda, Hedionda and Cañapa lagoons, then continues to the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and [Incahuasi Island](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/) with its giant cacti. Beyond the birdlife, the changing landscapes are remarkable: mineral lagoons, rocky desert stretches and the white salt surface.

The high-altitude section takes place far above sea level, with some sites around 4,400 m. Nights are colder here, and the weather may be very different from humid Iguazú. Stops included in the excursion program must be coordinated with actual conditions and driving times; health and tolerance of altitude are individual considerations. Compare [“Wildlife and Safaris” tours through Bolivia](/interests/wildlife/tours/bolivia/) for birdwatching possibilities, or the [“Nature” collection](/interests/nature/tours/bolivia/) for salt flats, mountains and geysers.

## Peru: Titicaca, mountain landscapes and realistic expectations

After Bolivia, travelers reach [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) and visit the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/). The program introduces the reed islands and the traditions of local residents. **A dedicated ornithological excursion on the lake is not included**, even though the natural setting is attractive in its own right.

The route then crosses the Andes to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). The archaeological complex lies amid mountain forests and steep slopes. On the current tours, the main purpose of this stop is to visit the Inca site and appreciate the surrounding landscape. It should not be marketed as an Inca Trail trek, a spectacled-bear-watching trip or a specialist natural-history excursion.

For travelers choosing a journey primarily for wildlife, this is an important compromise: Bolivia features explicitly named flamingos, Iguazú has a significant natural component, while Peru serves more as a cultural and scenic continuation. For Titicaca and mountain views, see [nature tours featuring Peru](/interests/nature/tours/peru/). If you select [“Wildlife and Safaris” tours featuring Peru](/interests/wildlife/tours/peru/), check the full program, including its other countries, for actual wildlife encounters.

## Which tours focus on wildlife and which on nature?

| Format | Thematic classification and focus |
|---|---|
| 18 days, 5 countries | Nature and culture: Iguazú and high-altitude lagoons, without a wildlife tag |
| 18 days with Carnival | Events, culture and natural stops; without a wildlife tag |
| 20 days, 6 countries | Nature and culture, additional stops; without a wildlife tag |
| 32 days, 8 countries | Wildlife as an additional theme: Bolivian flamingos and marine wildlife in Ecuador's Galápagos |

The [18-day five-country program](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) connects Iguazú, Chile, the Bolivian lagoons and Peru. The [20-day route](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) adds Uruguay. The [larger 32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) continues through Ecuador, where its Galápagos section includes alternative island excursions, and then proceeds to Colombia. **The Galápagos belong to Ecuador, not to the four selected countries**; they must not be included in descriptions of shorter five-country tours.

On programs featuring the [Champions Parade](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) and [New Year in Rio](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/), part of the schedule is determined by festive events. If your principal interests are flamingos, natural landscapes and photography, compare the duration of high-altitude days and actual excursions more closely than the festival date.

Explore other itineraries with scheduled wildlife experiences in the [multi-country “Wildlife and Safaris” selection](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/), and landscape-centered journeys in [“Nature”](/interests/nature/).

## Seasons, borders and expectations of wildlife encounters

A single journey combines the humid subtropical forests of Iguazú with the dry, cold highlands of Bolivia. Peru adds Lake Titicaca and mountain routes. Pack for each stage: waterproof protection at the falls, warm layers and sun protection at altitude, and comfortable shoes for long walks. The weather contrast within one trip is greater than the general label “South America” may suggest.

Visiting both sides of Iguazú requires a border crossing. The route later passes through Chile, even though the four-country filter does not list it, and then from Bolivia to Peru. Passport, entry and transit requirements must be checked for the nationalities and dates involved, rather than assuming one shared visa. Transport schedules and admission tickets also matter, especially when time at a natural attraction is limited.

Ada Tours helps coordinate the order of countries, excursion times and travel buffers. If you particularly want to observe a specific bird or animal, identify that goal from the outset: the mere presence of a national park cannot guarantee a sighting of a particular species.

## Frequently asked questions about wildlife in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil and Peru

### Where are flamingos mentioned in these tours?

In Bolivia, at [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). The itinerary identifies a habitat for James's flamingos but does not guarantee a sighting at a certain distance or in a specified number.

### Is a visit to the Iguazú Bird Park compulsory?

No. The [basic tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) lists the Bird Park as an optional activity. The main program includes the waterfalls.

### Does Peru have a dedicated wildlife safari?

The routes visit Titicaca, the Uros Islands, Cusco and Machu Picchu. No specialist safari or ornithological excursion is listed for these Peruvian days.

### Are the Galápagos included in the four-country program?

They feature only on the longer itinerary through Ecuador and other countries; they are not a separate stage of a route limited to Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil and Peru.

## Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Bolivia: how to combine four countries

The four countries cover very different parts of South America. In [Brazil](/brazil/), the itinerary begins with Rio de Janeiro and [Iguazú Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). In [Argentina](/argentina/), travelers explore the other side of Iguazú and Buenos Aires. From the Argentine capital they make a day trip to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), while in [Bolivia](/bolivia/) they cross high-altitude desert landscapes and the Uyuni Salt Flat.

Our catalog features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Both available itineraries include all four countries, but **neither is limited to them**. After Uruguay, the programs go through Santiago and the Atacama Desert in Chile, then Bolivia and Peru. The 32-day option continues into Ecuador and Colombia.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026,tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

{{#if catalog.hasComparableUsdPrice}}
The lowest comparable price in this collection is {{catalog.minUsdPriceLabel}}. It applies to a complete current program, not an independent four-country trip.
{{/if}}

This is especially important for transportation. The presence of Brazil and Bolivia in the same catalog does not mean there is a direct transfer from Iguazú to Uyuni. Buenos Aires, Uruguay and Chile lie between these sections of the itinerary.

## From the Atlantic coast to the salt flat: the travel sequence

| Country | What the itineraries actually include | Main logistical considerations |
|---|---|---|
| Brazil | Rio de Janeiro and the Brazilian side of Iguazú | Domestic flight and sightseeing days |
| Argentina | Argentine side of Iguazú, Buenos Aires | Border crossing at the falls and onward flights |
| Uruguay | Day trip to Montevideo from Buenos Aires | Return ferry, two border controls |
| Bolivia | Lagoons, Uyuni, La Paz, Tiwanaku | Jeeps, mountain roads, altitude and season |

The opening Brazilian section combines Rio city sightseeing with Iguazú. At the falls, travelers visit national parks on both sides of the border: the experiences complement each other, but entry rules and tickets differ by country. The Argentine portion then continues in Buenos Aires.

[Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) is the base for the Uruguay excursion. Tickets for the Buenos Aires – Montevideo – Buenos Aires ferry are included. Returning to the same country requires **re-entering Argentina**, and the evening schedule depends on the return ferry. An overnight stay in Uruguay or excursions to other parts of the country are not part of the standard itinerary.

Next comes a flight to Santiago, the road to San Pedro de Atacama and the high-altitude crossing into Bolivia. In the Bolivian section, participants travel in 4×4 vehicles past Laguna Verde, the Sol de Mañana geysers, reddish Laguna Colorada and other lakes before reaching the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and La Paz.

This chain explains why a small selection of countries in the page title corresponds to a long journey. The overall route is attractive if you want both cities and high-altitude nature; travelers seeking exactly four countries will need a newly planned set of flights.

## Two itineraries: what is the essential difference?

**“6 Latin American Countries in 20 Days”** ends in Lima. It travels from Rio and Iguazú via Buenos Aires, Montevideo, Chile, Bolivia and Peru to Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu. The description lists 4* hotels, domestic flights, specified excursions and the ferry to Uruguay. International flights are paid for separately. Full accommodation conditions and included services are set out in the [20-day program](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/).

**“8 South American Countries in 32 Days”** begins one day earlier, covers the same four selected countries and continues beyond Peru to Quito, the Galápagos, Medellín, Cartagena and Bogotá. It is designed for travelers prepared for a journey of more than a month and additional domestic flights. Check the exact daily itinerary, accommodation categories and price on the [32-day program page](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/).

The difference is not merely the 12 extra days. The longer route adds an island section with its own visitor requirements and complex logistics across Colombia. If Iguazú and Uyuni are your main interests, the shorter tour has fewer subsequent transfers; if you want to cross much of the continent in one journey, the longer one covers more territory.

## Documents and borders: entering Argentina twice and crossing Chile into Bolivia

At Iguazú, travelers cross the border between Brazil and Argentina. After taking a ferry from Buenos Aires to Montevideo, they pass Argentine entry control again on their return. Later, the itinerary enters Chile and crosses from the Atacama region into Bolivia. After Bolivia, the routes continue to Peru.

**For holders of a Russian international passport**, documents should be checked as of October 16, 2026, for the full journey, not only the four selected countries. The exact requirements depend on citizenship, passport validity, possible connections, purpose of stay and current government rules. Even where a separate tourist visa is not required, passport checks, maximum permitted stays and possible return-ticket requirements still apply.

Bolivia deserves particular attention. Travelers enter on a 4×4 journey from the San Pedro de Atacama area, rather than on an ordinary international flight into the capital. You therefore need to agree on **the exact border crossing, required documents and the meeting point with local transport**. Abandoning the organized transfer independently could disrupt subsequent overnight stays in the desert.

Brazil's Ministry of Health states that a vaccination certificate is not a blanket entry requirement for Brazil, but recommends that travelers assess yellow fever vaccination according to the regions they will visit; for recommended areas, vaccination is advised in advance. When the trip continues through Peru, and Ecuador and Colombia on the longer itinerary, health and certificate requirements must be considered across the entire sequence of crossings. Do not assume that one country's rules apply to its neighbors.

## Flights, ferry and jeeps: where to allow extra time

The most sensitive connections in this combination involve different forms of transport. **Flights within Brazil**, excursions on both sides of Iguazú, **the Buenos Aires – Montevideo – Buenos Aires ferry**, **flights to Santiago and Calama**, and **the Bolivian off-road route** each require different travel buffers.

For Uruguay, the return ferry time is critical. Adding an overnight stay changes the arrangements for the subsequent flight to Chile. In Bolivia, do not independently move the start of the jeep journey: the first section crosses remote highlands with limited alternative transport and an overnight stay in expedition-style accommodation.

When preparing a private version, we discuss the itinerary, connections and accommodation category, then recalculate transportation and included services. Simply dropping some countries does not guarantee a proportional price reduction: flights may become longer and group segments may have to be arranged privately.

## Money: four currencies and bank-card limitations

Each of the four countries has its own currency: **the Brazilian real**, **Argentine peso**, **Uruguayan peso** and **Bolivian boliviano**. US dollars can be useful as the pricing currency for the program and as a possible reserve, but that does not mean they are accepted everywhere in shops, markets or on public transport.

Before traveling, separate money by purpose: prepaid services, small daily expenses, optional excursions and a reserve for transport delays. Airport exchange rates may differ from city rates. Cash can be more practical than cards in smaller establishments and mountain areas of Bolivia.

**Cards issued by Russian banks cannot be assumed to work universally abroad.** Acceptance depends on the issuer, payment network and local bank. Withdrawal and conversion fees also vary. Check available payment methods in advance, especially if the journey continues beyond Bolivia to Peru and other countries.

## From Rio's heat to Uyuni's cold highlands

The climatic contrast is one of this four-country route's defining features. Rio and Iguazú call for lightweight clothing and protection against sun and humidity. Spring begins in Buenos Aires and Montevideo in late October, but exposed waterfronts can be windy. The San Pedro de Atacama region and Bolivian lagoons differ sharply from the ocean coast, with dry air, intense sunshine and cold mornings.

Some high-altitude sections reach well above 4,000 m. Traveling from low-lying cities to such elevations can cause altitude illness regardless of fitness. According to CDC guidance, the likelihood of problems depends on ascent rate and sleeping altitude; discuss your altitude tolerance and acclimatization plan with a physician before departure. If symptoms worsen, it is safer to stop ascending and seek medical help than to follow the timetable at any cost.

Pack light clothes, a warm midlayer, a wind-resistant jacket, comfortable shoes, sunglasses and a hat. Keep water and essentials close at hand during the off-road section. Check baggage allowances on each domestic flight and verify insurance coverage for the planned elevations and activities.

## Frequently asked questions about Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Bolivia

### Can I visit all four countries in 20 days?

The current 20-day program does include them, but it also visits Chile and Peru. Visiting only four countries would require a new plan for flights and overland transfers.

### Is there a direct route from Iguazú to Uyuni?

Not on the tours described. After Iguazú come Buenos Aires, a day trip to Uruguay and Chile. The Bolivian section begins near Atacama with a jeep journey.

### Why should I check requirements for re-entering Argentina?

Because after the first stay in Buenos Aires, travelers go to Montevideo and return to Argentina. Entry conditions and documents should be checked for both crossings.

### Is payment with a Russian bank card guaranteed?

No. Availability depends on the bank, payment network and country. Arrange a lawful backup payment method and check access to cash in advance.

### How demanding is the route for someone without high-altitude experience?

The high-altitude lagoons and Uyuni require attention to acclimatization and health. Before booking, discuss medical risks with a physician and possible adjustments to the pace or stages with Ada Tours.

### How do I choose between 20 and 32 days?

The 20-day option takes you through six countries as far as Peru. The 32-day version adds Ecuador, the Galápagos and Colombia. Your decision depends on available time, budget and willingness to undertake a long series of transfers.

## Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil and Uruguay: what adventures are actually included?

**The main active section of this combination takes place in high-altitude Bolivia.** The waterfalls on the Brazil–Argentina border offer walks beside immense cascades, while Uruguay appears as a separate city excursion from Buenos Aires. Four countries can be part of one journey, but not every stop involves sport or extreme activities.

Our collection features two extensive programs: [6 Latin American Countries in 20 Days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and [8 South American Countries in 32 Days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). **Both tours cover more countries than those named in this collection.** They also include Chile and Peru, while the extended version continues into Ecuador and Colombia. These four countries therefore represent the intersection of the itineraries, not a separate, consecutive four-country journey.

## From Iguazú Falls to high-altitude Bolivia

### Brazil and Argentina: two sides of one waterfall system

[Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) in Brazil and [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) in Argentina offer different views of the falls. The extensive 32-day tour visits both sides, first the Brazilian, then the Argentine, after which the group flies to Buenos Aires. The main activity is walking along developed trails and viewing platforms.

On the 32-day program, the Bird Park and Macuco Safari are listed as optional paid activities. It would be incorrect to describe the boat ride as an obligatory adventure on this tour. To enjoy Iguazú fully, allow time for both sides and a separate border crossing if they are included in the chosen itinerary.

### Bolivia: two days by jeep in the highlands

The most demanding part of the journey begins in Bolivia. From San Pedro de Atacama in Chile, the route crosses the border toward Laguna Verde, the Salvador Dalí Desert, the Polques hot springs and the Sol de Mañana geothermal area. Colorful lagoons, the Chiguana Salt Flat and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) follow. On the longer tour, this is **a two-day journey by 4×4 jeep** with an overnight stay in the high-altitude desert.

Some stretches lie above 4,000 m. This is a different challenge from walking around Iguazú Park: prolonged exposure to altitude, dry air, cold mornings, bumpy roads and distance from major settlements. Time in San Pedro de Atacama is used for acclimatization before the crossing. Before traveling, assess your altitude tolerance, health and ability to complete the planned journey, not just the beauty of the salt flat photographs.

An important distinction: **traveling by four-wheel-drive vehicle does not mean a multi-day hiking trek**. If you want a hike involving significant elevation gain, you should not assume it is included merely because the tour has an “Adventure” tag.

## What Argentina and Uruguay offer between the nature sections

After Iguazú, the route leads to Buenos Aires and from there to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). This involves a ferry crossing of the Río de la Plata estuary and sightseeing in Uruguay's capital, with a return to Buenos Aires the same day. On both the 20- and 32-day programs, it provides a city-focused interval between natural attractions and the more demanding Andean stage.

There is no separate rafting, trekking or expedition-style off-road activity here. Uruguay's value in this combination is discovering Montevideo and traveling across the estuary, but a sports activity must not be added to the description without confirmation in the itinerary.

In Buenos Aires, the principal activities are sightseeing in historic neighborhoods and discovering tango. If you are more interested in this than extreme activities, see the separate [cultural and historical tours featuring Argentina](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/argentina/).

## Comparing the 20- and 32-day itineraries

| Program | Main difference |
|---|---|
| [20 days, 6 countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) | Compact chain: Iguazú – capitals – Atacama and Uyuni – Peru |
| [32 days, 8 countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) | The same major Andean section plus Ecuador, Galápagos and Colombia |

Both itineraries include an intensive Andean section. The longer one allows you to see much more of South America but adds flights and a longer overall trip. For someone traveling mainly for high-altitude scenery, extra countries do not replace days at Uyuni. Compare the actual stops and overnight conditions rather than just the total number of destinations.

Seasonal conditions at the waterfalls and in high-altitude Bolivia are fundamentally different. Iguazú is warm and humid; the Altiplano can bring strong winds, low temperatures and sharp changes even within a single day. Warm layers, sun protection and reliable footwear are essential. Medical contraindications to being at altitude should be discussed before the mountain section.

## Why combine these particular countries?

Brazil and Argentina share one natural attraction seen from opposite sides of the border. Bolivia replaces the familiar tropical setting with lagoons, high-altitude desert and salt flats. Uruguay adds a short city excursion during a stay in Buenos Aires. The combination therefore suits travelers who want **one extensive journey with contrasting nature and cultural days**, not a nonstop active tour without breaks.

For a narrower choice of high-altitude programs, see [adventure tours featuring Bolivia](/interests/adventure/tours/bolivia/) and the [general adventure collection](/interests/adventure/). When selecting dates, check the actual daily route, altitude and activities included.

## Frequently asked questions about adventures across four countries

### Do I need to be an experienced mountaineer to visit Uyuni?

Mountaineering experience is not specified for the jeep route described. Nevertheless, elevations above 4,000 m can seriously affect how you feel even without strenuous exercise. Altitude preparation and individual medical limitations matter more than athletic experience.

### Is the boat safari at Iguazú included in the tour?

On the 32-day program, Macuco Safari is listed as an optional paid activity. Distinguish the basic waterfall visits on both sides from the optional boat ride.

### Will there be a separate outdoor adventure in Uruguay?

On these programs, Uruguay is represented by Montevideo, reached by a return ferry trip from Buenos Aires. No hiking or off-road nature adventure in Uruguay is specified.

## What cultural experiences connect these four countries?

Our collection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Both available itineraries travel through Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil and Uruguay but **are not limited to these countries**. The [20-day tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) includes 6 countries and the [32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) includes 8. Travelers also visit Chile between Uruguay and Bolivia, and then continue into Peru.

The four countries' cultural attractions can be divided into several stories: historic buildings in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), urban neighborhoods and tango in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), the port heritage of [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), and the monuments of [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/). Their differences are far more interesting than a simple count of visited countries.

## Brazil and Argentina: from old streets to tango

In Rio, the program includes an excursion to Corcovado through [Tijuca Forest](/brazil/place/tijuca-national-park/), as well as Sugarloaf Mountain and central city districts. The urban portion of the second day introduces old churches, monasteries and colonial buildings. This is a sightseeing format lasting a few hours, not a multi-day expedition through Brazil's architectural monuments. Other cultural programs are available in the [Brazil thematic collection](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/brazil/).

In Buenos Aires, sightseeing with a Russian-speaking guide is scheduled. The route goes through [La Boca](/argentina/place/la-boca/), [San Telmo](/argentina/place/san-telmo/), Plaza de Mayo and Recoleta. This allows visitors to compare the city's port history, administrative center and later neighborhoods. Both itineraries include a tango show with dinner in the evening. This is part of the tour; tango lessons or attendance at a festival are not listed.

Between Rio and Buenos Aires lie the waterfalls near [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). This is a substantial natural stop, but it should not be treated as an excursion into the history of Argentina or Brazil.

## Uruguay: discovering Montevideo in one day

Both programs include a return ferry trip from Buenos Aires to Montevideo. The excursion covers the port, Independence Square, the [Old Town](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/) and the cathedral. After sightseeing, there is free time before returning to Argentina.

This is an opportunity to compare two capitals on opposite sides of the Río de la Plata. However, the itineraries discussed do not include an overnight stay in Uruguay. One day will be too short to explore Montevideo's museums at a relaxed pace or visit other historic towns in Uruguay. If that is your principal aim, look for a longer stay.

## Bolivia: from urban La Paz to Tiwanaku

In [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), a city tour includes the market and urban landmarks. An excursion to [Valley of the Moon](/bolivia/place/moon-valley-la-paz/) complements it, with the natural rock formations as the principal attraction.

Tiwanaku opens a very different chapter in South American history. The archaeological tour visits the complex, including the Gate of the Sun and Kalasasaya. Here travelers encounter physical monuments of a culture that flourished before the Inca period. The contrast with colonial cities is particularly important to the cultural theme of the journey.

However, Tiwanaku is visited as part of the drive from La Paz toward the Peruvian border. The route then continues to Lake Titicaca. The itinerary therefore does not allow extensive independent exploration of excavations, museums and additional monuments.

## Why the four countries cannot be combined in an arbitrary order

The actual sequence is Rio and Iguazú, Buenos Aires, a day trip to Montevideo and back, a flight to Santiago, the Atacama section, then high-altitude Bolivia and Peru. **Chile lies between Uruguay and Bolivia** on both current tours, even though the thematic collection selects a different group of four countries.

After coastal and lowland cities, travelers reach high-altitude conditions. For a cultural excursion to Tiwanaku, this means allowing for acclimatization and long transfers. Border-crossing documents and entry rules should be checked against the travelers' nationalities, the complete list of countries and the second entry into Argentina after Uruguay.

### Is there a ready-made itinerary covering only these four countries?

The current collection has no separate ready-made journey exclusively through these four countries. Both available tours also travel through Chile and Peru.

### Are tango and Tiwanaku included?

Yes. The programs include a tango show with dinner in Buenos Aires; Tiwanaku is visited on the way from La Paz to the Peruvian border.
